doc: The gradient selector on h & 15: for h = 0..15 with (x, y, z) = (0.3, 0.5, 0.7) the 16 results are {+-x or +-y, +-y or +-x or +-z} per the improved-Perlin table: u = x if h < 8 else y; v = y if h < 4, x if h in {12, 14}, else z; the sign of u flips on bit 0 of h and the sign of v on bit 1. The following rows use h = 16..47 and 240..255 (the mask & 15 must wrap them) with random coordinates. One float32 addition of two selected, possibly negated inputs: bit-identical in any float32 implementation; the tolerance (1e-6 rel) is only slack for a port that computes in float64.
